question: Which of the following rivers is NOT the part of Sapta-Sindhu, the region where early Vedic Aryans lived?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagirathi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The early Vedic Aryans lived in the area known as Sapta-Sindhu meaning an area of seven rivers.
 
• Sapta-Sindhu meaning 7 rivers are the term that gave birth to the word “Hindu”.
 
• It was referred to as Hapta-Hindu by Persians etc.
 
• This area largely covers the northwestern part of South Asia up to river Yamuna.
 
• The seven rivers included Sindhu (Indus), Vitasta (Jhelum), Asikni (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipash (Beas), Shutudri (Sutlej), and the Sarasvati. Hence option 3 is correct.
 
• In this area, the Rigvedic people lived, fought battles, grazed their herds of cattle and other domesticated animals.
 
• Gradually moving eastward, they came to occupy eastern U.P. (Kosala) and north Bihar (Videha) during the Later Vedic period.
 
• The Sapta Saindhavas country of the Rig Vedic period was bounded by the Himalayas and modern Tibet in the east, Turkistan in the north, Afghanistan, in the west, and the Aravallis in the south.
